question: What changed in the latest Fortnite update?

receipts.question: What changed in the latest Fortnite update?
receipts.answer:
The newest update the sources detail in full is v43.00, but only its creator-side (UEFN) changes are covered. It brings Procedural Content Generation to UEFN, more MCP workflows for profiling, cinematics, audio and animation, and takes the Progression API out of Experimental so islands can publish custom quests [5]. It also adds Frenzy Fields prefabs and galleries, plus new HUD Controller options such as overriding Interact and Pickup [5]. The sources don't include v43.00 player-facing patch notes, such as new weapons or map changes.

A newer update, v43.10, is mentioned as upcoming as of November 5, 2026, and will let Batman appear as a night-time visitor in LEGO Fortnite villages [6]. Separately, a Treasure Hunters mini-season launched November 1 with a One Piece collaboration, custom Pirate Crews and a new Battle Pass [7][6].

For the last battle royale patch with full notes, v42.40 (October 15, 2026) added Loot Hacks including the Gatekeeper Shotgun and Hunting Rifle, and two new Sprites, Honey and One Wish Willow [1]. It also vaulted several Hacks, slightly increased the Sweeper Shotgun's fire rate, and fixed AMD launch crashes [1].

question: What are the biggest video game releases this month?

receipts.question: What are the biggest video game releases this month?
receipts.answer:
The two biggest November 2026 releases are Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox, and the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time [1]. GTA 6 is the month's dominant release, and Eurogamer says the Ocarina of Time Remake arrives early in the month [3]. Polygon notes that GTA 6 isn't coming to Switch 2, and describes the Zelda remake as Nintendo's counter-programming [7].

Other notable releases include:
- Shrek 2 Remastered and Warhammer Survivors on November 10 [1]. Warhammer Survivors will also be a day-one Xbox Game Pass release [2].
- Football Manager 27 on November 10 [2].
- Barbie Rewind, Metaphor: ReFantazio (Switch 2), Pikmin 4 Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy, and Sonic Pico Park on November 12 [1].
- Gothic 3 Classic on November 24 [1].

Two outlets say the month is lighter than usual because of GTA 6. IGN says there are relatively few releases compared with the past two months [8], and Polygon says many developers moved their games out of November [7].

question: What are the CDC's current COVID-19 vaccine recommendations for adults?

receipts.question: What are the CDC's current COVID-19 vaccine recommendations for adults?
receipts.answer:
CDC currently recommends a 2026-2027 COVID-19 vaccine for all adults ages 18 years and older, per guidance dated September 23, 2026 [1][6]. The recommended vaccine and number of doses depend on age, vaccination history, and immune status [1].

- **Ages 12-64 who were previously vaccinated:** 1 dose of a Moderna, Novavax, or Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, at least 8 weeks after the last dose (or at least 3 months for Moderna mNexspike) [1].
- **Ages 65 and older:** 2 doses, with the second given 6 months after the first (minimum interval 2 months, or 3 months for mNexspike) [1].
- **Moderately or severely immunocompromised people:** a modified schedule applies [7].
- **Prior infection:** a 2026-2027 vaccine is recommended even if you already had COVID-19 [6].

There is a source discrepancy. One CDC overview page still describes adult vaccination as individual-based (shared clinical) decision-making and refers to 2025-2026 vaccines [3]. The newer September 2026 guidance instead recommends vaccination for all adults [1]. Another CDC page says the July 2025 immunization schedule recommendations remain in effect for the 2026-2027 season because of legal uncertainties [5].

CDC also says all patients should discuss the benefits and risks of vaccination with their healthcare provider to make personalized decisions [5]. Personal medical decisions belong with a clinician.

question: Is there a measles outbreak in the United States right now?

receipts.question: Is there a measles outbreak in the United States right now?
receipts.answer:
CDC data show measles cases and outbreaks have been reported in the United States in 2026, though the sources give different figures for the exact count [8][1].

The most recent snippet with a case total (dated September 23, 2026) says 3,471 confirmed cases had been reported as of September 17, 2026, with 39 new outbreaks reported in 2026, and 95% of cases (3,296 of 3,471) were outbreak-associated [8]. Two other pages carry an older count of 2,465 confirmed cases and 38 new outbreaks, and they are labeled "Updated on August 7, 2026" [1][3]. One CDC page says it was updated November 6, 2026, but its excerpt does not include the 2026 case total [2].

CDC defines an outbreak as 3 or more related cases, and states have the most current information on local cases and outbreaks [2]. CDC says outbreaks can occur when measles reaches communities of unvaccinated people [2]. Kindergarten MMR coverage was 92.4% in 2025–2026, down from 95.2% in 2019–2020 [2].

For current local risk or personal medical decisions, check your state health department and talk with a clinician.

question: Who should get a flu shot this season, according to the CDC?

receipts.question: Who should get a flu shot this season, according to the CDC?
receipts.answer:
CDC recommends an annual flu vaccine for everyone aged 6 months and older who does not have a contraindication, with rare exceptions [4][5]. This applies to the 2026-2027 season, for which CDC says the recommendations from the July 2025 immunization schedule remain in effect [3].

- **Higher-risk groups:** CDC lists young children, pregnant women, people with chronic conditions such as asthma, diabetes, or heart and lung disease, and people 65 and older as being at higher risk of serious flu complications [6]. Vaccination is also important for health care workers and others who live with or care for higher-risk people [6].
- **Pregnancy:** Women who are pregnant or will be pregnant during flu season should get vaccinated, and during pregnancy they should get the flu shot rather than the nasal spray [4].
- **Infants:** Children younger than 6 months are at higher risk but are too young to be vaccinated [6].
- **Age 65 and older:** Three flu vaccines are preferentially recommended for this group [5].
- **Timing:** CDC says vaccination is ideally done by the end of October, but people should keep getting vaccinated as long as flu viruses threaten their community [6].

Which vaccine is appropriate depends on age and health, and personal medical decisions belong with a clinician [5].

question: What are the most recent discoveries from the James Webb Space Telescope?

receipts.question: What are the most recent discoveries from the James Webb Space Telescope?
receipts.answer:
The most recent Webb-related result in these sources is a new image-processing technique, reported November 10, 2026, that uncovered a previously hidden exoplanet in existing Webb data. Caltech researchers built a digital twin of Webb's NIRCam, called FLIP, that removes starlight and made faint planets two to 15 times easier to detect than conventional methods in tests with known planets [2]. A Nature study on the software is covered by Scientific American (November 4), where an outside expert called the result significant [4]. Webb can currently detect Saturn-sized worlds orbiting farther out than Pluto does around our sun, and Earth-sized planets would need a telescope 100 to 1,000 times more stable [4].

Other recent findings:
- **Lopsided atmosphere (October 2026):** Webb found that the atmosphere of the gas giant WASP-17b, 1,300 light-years away, bulges on one side because powerful winds redistribute heat. This comes from a snippet only [6].
- **Dark matter in an ancient galaxy cluster (presented June 17, 2026):** Webb revealed that the cluster XLSSC 122, about 10.4 billion light-years away, has an unexpectedly dense concentration of dark matter, which challenges theories of how the universe developed. This also comes from a snippet only [7].
- **Organic molecules (February 2026):** Webb detected benzene, methane and the methyl radical in the buried core of the galaxy IRAS 07251-0248. It was the first detection of the methyl radical beyond the Milky Way [3].

NASA's Webb news page also lists items such as a giant exoplanet hiding in data, a first stellar-mass black hole located using Hubble archival data, and a Webb view of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, but the excerpts give no detail on these [1][5].

question: Is 2026 on track to be one of the hottest years on record?

receipts.question: Is 2026 on track to be one of the hottest years on record?
receipts.answer:
Yes. The WMO says 2026 is set to be one of the four hottest years on record, with January–September averaging about 1.47 °C above the 1850–1900 average and likely to rise by year's end as El Niño intensifies [1]. NOAA's September outlook (published October 2026) said it is very likely 2026 will rank among the five warmest years, most probably second-warmest [6]. Copernicus said in its November 6 bulletin that 2026 is most likely to be second-hottest, with a 20% chance of tying or exceeding 2024's record [2].

Copernicus gives 2026 a 20% chance of tying or exceeding 2024, while Scientific American says 2026 could set the record for hottest year [2][5]. Scientific American's projection puts 2026 at 1.52 °C above preindustrial and says it could surpass 2024, though 2027 is "virtually certain" to take the crown [5]. The WMO notes that January–September 2026 is still below the 2024 record of 1.55 °C [1].

question: What is the current federal minimum wage in the United States?

receipts.question: What is the current federal minimum wage in the United States?
receipts.answer:
The current federal minimum wage under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) is $7.25 per hour, as stated in a January 5, 2026 Wage and Hour Division opinion letter [3] and in the Department of Labor's table of minimum wages, last revised July 1, 2026 [4]. The same DOL table lists a maximum tip credit of $5.12 and a minimum cash wage of $2.13 for tipped employees under the FLSA [4].

Don't confuse this with the higher rates for certain federal contractors. Under Executive Order 13658, the rate is $13.65 per hour from May 11, 2026 [1], rising to $14.05 on January 6, 2027 [2]. Those rates apply only to certain older federal contracts, not to workers generally [1][2].

A bill to raise the federal minimum wage (H.R. 8555, the Living Wage For All Act) was introduced April 28, 2026 and referred to committee; the sources show it only as introduced, not enacted [5].

This covers U.S. federal law only. Many states set higher minimums, and rules differ by jurisdiction [3][4]. This is general legal information, not legal advice; a specific situation needs a licensed lawyer.

The Commission's AI Office has been able to enforce those rules since 2 August 2026, when its enforcement powers began to apply [1][6][7]. A U.S. Congressional Research Service report (undated, and shown only as partial snippets) says GPAI transparency rules apply from August 2025, which matches the above [8]. The newer EU sources say high-risk rules for Annex III systems now apply from 2 December 2027, after amendment by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 [1][4].

question: What are the current TSA rules for liquids in carry-on bags?

receipts.question: What are the current TSA rules for liquids in carry-on bags?
receipts.answer:
Liquids, aerosols and gels in carry-on bags must be 3.4 ounces (100 mL) or less each [3]. Under the 3-1-1 rule, they must also fit in one quart-sized, resealable bag [6]. Larger amounts of things you can spill, spread, spray, pump or pour, including foods like sauces, jam, preserves and wine, belong in checked bags [3].

- **Exceptions:** Medically necessary liquids over 3.4 ounces are allowed in reasonable quantities for your flight. You must tell the officer at the start of screening, and they may be screened further, including being opened [3][7]. Liquids associated with nebulizers are also exempt from the 3-1-1 rule in reasonable quantities [5].
- **CT lanes:** At checkpoints with CT scanners, passengers don't need to remove their 3-1-1 liquids from their carry-on bags [1].
- **Hand sanitizer:** Sources from 2021 and 2022 say one container of up to 12 ounces of liquid hand sanitizer was allowed in carry-ons due to the pandemic, "until further notice" [4][6][8].

question: Do US citizens need a visa to visit Japan for tourism?

receipts.question: Do US citizens need a visa to visit Japan for tourism?
receipts.answer:
No. US citizens can visit Japan for tourism without a visa. As of October 2026, Americans on a US passport enter visa-free, and Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists the United States among its visa-exempt countries and regions [5]. The standard stay is up to 90 days, which covers tourism and unpaid business activities [5]. The State Department's Japan advisory (issued September 28, 2026) likewise describes tourist or business "visa free" stays of up to 90 days [2].

- **Passport:** It should be valid for your whole stay and have a blank page for the entry stamp [5].
- **Work:** Working on a tourist entry is not allowed [2][5].
- **Extensions:** These are granted only in exceptional cases, such as humanitarian reasons [5].
- **Visit Japan Web:** It is free and recommended, but not mandatory [5].
- **JESTA:** This planned electronic travel authorization is not yet in force, so you don't need it for trips today [5].

Since the sources point to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan as the authority for entry rules, confirm there before you book [3]. I have only secondary summaries of that guidance, not the ministry's own page.

question: What internal temperature does the USDA recommend for cooking chicken?

receipts.question: What internal temperature does the USDA recommend for cooking chicken?
receipts.answer: The USDA recommends cooking chicken to an internal temperature of 165°F [7][6]. USDA's FSIS lists 165°F for poultry, and a Serious Eats piece says the USDA calls 165°F the safe minimum internal temperature for all poultry [7][6]. CDC and FDA guidance agree, and CDC says to confirm the temperature with a food thermometer rather than color or texture [3][4]. Serious Eats (April 2026) argues that white meat can be safe below 165°F if held at a lower temperature long enough, but it calls 165°F the simplest, most foolproof rule and says this is not the official guidance [1].

question: When does the 2027-28 FAFSA open, and what changed?

receipts.question: When does the 2027-28 FAFSA open, and what changed?
receipts.answer:
The 2027-28 FAFSA is already open: the Department of Education announced on September 23, 2026 that the form was online and available, its earliest launch in program history for the second year in a row [1]. The paper form says federal aid applications can be submitted no earlier than October 1, 2026, and must be received by June 30, 2028 [2]. The statutory deadline for launch was October 1 [1].

What changed, per the Department:
- Questions and instructions were rewritten in clearer language [1].
- Students can invite a contributor by text message as well as email [1].
- Returning students' data is to be pre-populated from previous FAFSA forms "later this fall" [1]. The Specifications Guide (September 2026) says renewal applications will be offered this cycle, but the implementation date had not been confirmed [3].
- The Specifications Guide also notes significant changes to questions on the online and PDF forms [3].

Features introduced in the previous cycle and carried forward include:
- Real-time Pell Grant and aid eligibility results [1].
- Reuse of parent information across multiple children's applications [1].
- Simpler contributor invitations, by code or QR code [1][4].
- An earnings indicator showing whether a school's graduates earn less than a high-school graduate [1].

The Department also says it has strengthened fraud prevention [1].

question: What's new in the latest version of Blender?

receipts.question: What's new in the latest version of Blender?
receipts.answer:
Blender 5.3, released November 10, 2026, is the latest version, and its release page lists new features across viewport, animation, and editing tools [1].

- **Viewport and GPU:** There's a new DLSS denoiser for the viewport on NVIDIA GPUs, native support for NVIDIA RTX Spark devices running Windows 11, and Vulkan as the default backend on Windows (except ARM) and Linux. Workbench can also use hardware raytraced shadows on Metal and Vulkan [1].
- **Grease Pencil:** Draw Mode gets selection tools, plus a new Carver Tool for boolean-subtraction cuts. The Fill tool can now fill many regions at once [1].
- **Video Sequencer:** It gains a full ripple editing framework, a rewritten blade tool, and initial OpenTimelineIO support [1].
- **Project system:** A new optional project system makes Blender aware of context beyond the open .blend file [1].
- **Animation & Rigging:** There are new operators to copy and paste world-space animation and to convert rotation modes, along with friendlier playback [1].

The release page excerpt is a summary, and it points to the full release notes for the complete list [1].

- **Creative Agent:** Adobe is expanding the Adobe Creative Agent across Creative Cloud and Firefly, so creatives can hand off complex, multi-step tasks by directing it in their own words. [1]

- **Firefly:** Adobe introduced new video, audio, image and design tools, a choice of top industry AI models, and the Creative Agent in one place. [1] Firefly Design (beta) and Firefly Graph (beta) are new, and Firefly Builder is in private beta preview. [3]
- **Creative Cloud:** New features include Relight in Photoshop and Color Mode in Premiere. [1] Photoshop also gets Generative Restyle. [3]
- **GenStudio:** CX Enterprise Coworker is coming to GenStudio to help teams manage campaign workflows through a conversational interface. [1] Firefly 3D Digital Twin will let teams and AI agents change a product's labels and materials and generate product images without a new photoshoot. [1]
- **Partnerships:** Adobe is deepening its partnerships with Google and Microsoft. [1] It also announced a multi-year strategic alliance with The Walt Disney Company, as Official AI Innovation Partner. [1]

question: What is the US Copyright Office's current position on AI-generated art?

receipts.question: What is the US Copyright Office's current position on AI-generated art?
receipts.answer:
In the Review Board's decision on Théâtre D'opéra Spatial, the Copyright Office treated AI-generated material as something that must be disclaimed in a registration application, and it accepted that human-authored contributions could be registered [3]. In the 2023 Théâtre D'opéra Spatial decision, the Review Board affirmed refusal because the work contained more than a de minimis amount of AI-generated content that had to be disclaimed, and the applicant was unwilling to disclaim it [3]. The Office had earlier said the Midjourney-generated image forming the basis of that work was not an original work of authorship protected by copyright, but it accepted that human-authored Photoshop edits could contain enough original authorship to be registered [3]. The Board added that if the applicant were willing to disclaim the AI-generated material, he could file a new application and explain why his modifications amount to copyrightable authorship [3].

The Office's formal analysis is in Part 2 of its AI report, published January 29, 2025, which addresses the copyrightability of outputs created using generative AI [4]. The excerpt of that report available here doesn't state its conclusions, so I can't summarize them beyond that [6]. The Office also held a June 28, 2023 webinar on registration guidance for works containing AI-generated content [4].
